messages:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Dedicated pool 'ded-vpc-42' reported GPU node failure (node-7g). Severity: P2. Auto-drain started.

maria-eng: seeing the same in metrics — GPU temp spiked then ECC errors. node-7g disabled from scheduler automatically.

ajay-oncall: I'm paged and looking. Can someone confirm which customers are on ded-vpc-42?

ryan-sre: pulling allocation map now. customer tenancy pinned: elliot-corp (3 instances), internal-canary (2), batch-job-queue (1).

ryan-sre: elliot-corp is on strict VPC + private-networking; can't live-migrate without their ACLs.

sophia-custsuccess: pinging Elliot SRE (elliot-corp-sre) now — they're on standby for any IP/route changes.

elliot-corp-sre: confirmed we see degraded perf from our side for model-serving replicas (inference tail latency up ~6x). We're ready to accept traffic shift if you need us to flip routing.

maria-eng: quick status: node shows hardware ECC and a kernel oops during GPU init. Logs: ```
[  +0.000000] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:02:00): 79, pid=0, GPU is unreachable
[  +0.001234] nvidia: GPU lockup - resetting
[  +0.002345] kworker/3:3: segfault at 0 ip 00007f...```

ajay-oncall: plan proposal: 1) finish automated drain on node-7g, 2) cordon node, 3) spin up replacement in same AZ from spare pool, 4) for elliot-corp, create temporary dedicated slice on ded-vpc-burst and update their LB to route to new replicas behind feature-flag. Any objections?

ryan-sre: agree, but note: elliot-corp has a VPC peering acl that only allows specific subnets. We'll need to ensure replacement slice carries same VPC tags or do NAT/route-based workaround. That requires a short config change on their end.

sophia-custsuccess: Elliots says they can add the subnet for 10.7.22.0/24 if needed, but want a heads-up for compliance logging.

ajay-oncall: marking action items: (A) maria to complete drain and attach logs, (B) ryan to provision replacement node and ensure VPC tags, (C) sophia to coordinate with elliot-corp-sre for subnet addition, (D) i will monitor SLOs and hold postmortem.

maria-eng: running drain command now: ```kubectl drain node-7g --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force``` Should prevent further scheduling. I'll paste pod eviction logs when done.

maria-eng: eviction summary: evicted 6 pods (3 elliot-corp replicas, 2 internal-canary, 1 batch). Starting reschedule to ded-vpc-burst.

deploy-bot: Deploy triggered: create-replacement-node --pool=ded-vpc-burst --az=us-east-1a --gpu-type=a100 --tags="vpc:ded-vpc-42" --reason="hot-replace node-7g" (task id: t-88f2)

ryan-sre: replacement node provisioned (node-rp3). attaching host route and vpc-tag. Running kube join then taint removal.

ryan-sre: runbook note — because elliot-corp requires private model keys, do NOT migrate replicas that reference customer KMS keys to any unvetted host. We'll create new replicas but ensure KMS endpoint is only accessible via allowed subnet.

ajay-oncall: status update for stakeholders: impact: 3 of Elliot Corp's serving replicas down for ~8m during drain; tail latency elevated for their customers. No data loss. Currently routing to new replicas in ded-vpc-burst after subnet confirmation from Elliot.

sophia-custsuccess: communicated to Elliot: "we're shifting a small number of replicas to a temporary slice in our burst pool; this is short-lived and we'll migrate back once hardware replaced. We'll provide audit logs for compliance." They acknowledged.

maria-eng: hardware team requested node pulled for post-mortem; I attached fault dump to ticket HW-5219. Looks like a memory channel issue on GPU board. Recommend RMA.

ryan-sre: monitoring: node-rp3 and rescheduled pods are healthy. Per-route p99 now back to baseline for Elliot. Continuing to watch for 30m.

ajay-oncall: closing immediate mitigation. Severity drop to P3. Still tracking replacement and RMA. Sophia, please draft a short customer update for legal/compliance.

sophia-custsuccess: drafting now. Will include timeline, KMS access note, and audit logs. ETA 10m.

elliot-corp-sre: thanks for the fast response. Please keep our SOC in the loop for any key-access changes.

maria-eng: postmortem notes (to seed): root cause: GPU board ECC/fatal during init; auto-drain prevented noisy restart storm. Mitigation: replacement and RMA; action: add an early-warning metric for ECC count threshold to trigger preemptive replacement.

ajay-oncall: handoff to night oncall @ryan-sre: please pick up monitoring and ensure RMA ticket progresses. Key items for handoff: - replacement node stability - confirm all elliot replicas on original pool after RMA - close HW-5219 after RMA and attach audit logs.

ryan-sre: acked. I'll follow up with HW team and set a maintenance window for returning elliot-corp to original pool.

ops-bot: Incident note recorded: incident-id INC-2026-6187. Timeline, actions, and participants archived.

ajay-oncall: final check: does anyone see outstanding customer-facing items? If not we mark mitigated and continue RMA tracking offline.

sophia-custsuccess: final: customer update sent; legal copied. Marking mitigated for now. :white_check_mark:

ryan-sre: leaving short handoff message for next oncall: "watch for repeat ECC spikes across same rack (r-11), if >2 occurrences within 24h, start pro-evac plan for rack."

maria-eng: adding the ECC alert to the metrics board and will propose a quantized threshold in the follow-up postmortem.
